gaps.after: The loser never says what will happen: it shows only 'Repeats Periodically' and 'Days after completion 7' as a bare right-edge value, with no next-date line. The winner names the kind 'After Completion', puts the interval in a filled ~28px number field with a 'days' unit menu, and adds a muted ~13px 'Done today? Next: Sun, Oct 23' line, so the rule reads at a glance. Add that preview line and replace the vague 'Periodically'.
gaps.weekly: The loser's weekday row is seven bare ~16px checkboxes over single-letter labels (S M T W T F S). The two S's and two T's are ambiguous and the checkboxes read as a web form. The winner uses a ~40x30px segmented chip row with three-letter names (Sun...Sat), fills the selected Fri in solid blue, and adds a 'Next: Fri, Oct 6' preview line.
gaps.monthly: The loser's dimmed 'On day' row shows the value 'Last', so it reads 'On day Last', which means nothing, and there is no next-date line. The winner shows a concrete '29th' in the dimmed On day row and a muted ~13px 'Next: Fri, Oct 27' line under Ends, so the result is explicit.
gaps.kinds: The loser's menu is a generic popup of bare kind names on ~58px rows (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Yearly, Periodically) with no hint of what each would produce. The winner lists each kind on ~34px rows with a right-aligned grey preview ('Every day', 'Fridays', 'The 29th', 'Sep 29', 'Every 2 weeks') and sets After Completion ('1 week') apart below a hairline divider.
gaps.phone: The loser crams label and value into one row, so the 'Repeat' label truncates to 'R...' next to '4 days after completion'. The winner gives Repeat its own full-width row (~17pt label, 'After Completion' value menu), then 'Every [4] days', 'Ends Never' and a muted 'Done today? Next: Mon, Apr 1' line.

why: Deciding factor: whether each state spells out the outcome. Next-date lines, full weekday names and per-kind previews beat the vague 'Periodically', single-letter checkboxes and a label truncated to 'R...'.
